hyps.why: Raising an already large Adam learning rate causes divergence, unlike raising a small one.
Tiny learning rates leave the MLP undertrained in 243 epochs, so increasing them helps substantially.
Reducing an unstable learning rate recovers accuracy, whereas reducing a moderate one does not.
Shrinking an already tiny learning rate worsens underfitting.
Extra L2 penalty only matters once alpha is large, where it causes severe underfitting.
Relaxing a heavy L2 penalty restores capacity, while relaxing a negligible one changes nothing.
Larger batches mean fewer updates, compounding the slow progress of a small learning rate.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilize training at aggressive learning rates.
With large batches there are few updates per epoch, so a bigger step size is more beneficial and better tolerated.
Deeper ReLU networks are more prone to instability and dead units at large learning rates.
